institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was more than crucial to find a study destination with the perfect intersection between academic opportunities and fascinating culture/city. As I already spoke a little French before arriving, I found that Paris and Sciences Po was the perfect match for me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I must say that I found the process very demanding and for the most of the time you're left alone as a student. However, after the formel submission and application to Sciences Po, the process went smooth.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received the necessary information by e-mail.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very hard. Paris is a city with a lack of student housing, and unfortunately a lot of scammers seek to take advantages of this. I ended up living in student housing, but would have enjoyed living in the city centre.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You will be spending some time taking the metro.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The process was easy to understand, but seemed very unmanageable as Sciences Po has a "first come, first serve"-principle.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had a number of opportunities available at 4 pm. When clock reached exactly 4, you had to choose your preferred courses. However, you had to prioritize your time as they did it by first come, first serve.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Informational videos.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had two courses that I wasn't able to get, but I was satisfied overall.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take your time to prioritize the courses before 4 pm. Make a plan for what you will choose if some courses aren't available.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level at Sciences Po in itself is not higher than in UCPH. However, the work load is out of this world with assessment to be done every 3-4 days during the 4 months. I ended up having 18 assessments throughout the year.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At Sciences Po we had smaller lectures with more interaction with the teachers. That was something that reminded me of High School and it served to be very beneficial.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: A lot of the nights out and "soirées" are rather expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffeeshops in Paris hold the same prices in Denmark. Going out for dinner is actually a little cheaper. The food in the cantina at Sciences Po is half the price of UCPH.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You had a variety of activities to choose from (courses).

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything from wine tasting to football.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you enjoy sports, enroll yourself in a sports class. it's such an easy way to get friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Canal St-Matin and have a glass of wine. The Canal is way less crowded than the Seine.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The Parisian culture is not far from the one of Copenhagen.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Local Parisian students run their own show. They are faced with heavy workloads from working and studying so many of them keep themselves away from exchange students. However, most are very kind and are from my experience very kind to help with language difficulties.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
A lot of homeless people in Paris. Can be difficult to deal with as a scandi. 
Also there was a lot of demonstrations and strikes during my stay which paralyzed the public transportation.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Wine & chill culture, meaning that people in Paris can sit outside of the bistros and drink wine all night without getting absolutely drunk. That differs a lot from the danish drinking culture, I find.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do everything you can to find a studio in the city centre. 
They expect you to do A LOT of work, but they don't expect the same academic levels at UCPH. 
Try to get out of your comfort zone, and find international friends by joining the welcome programme.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: As I've mentioned a couple of times, don't worry about the workload. They prefer quantity over quality.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Exploring new cultures and getting international friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: As I also followed a French class (in which we can't get transferred the ECTS from to UCPH) I ended up taking 34 ECTS points. 34 ECTS points at Sciences Po is more than challenging, and as you also want your exchange experience to be a social experience, some days are tough and late.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
